stem: Which record is most interpretable later?

stimulus.title: Measurement event context
stimulus.description: A technician is documenting a completed input-solution conductivity check. Select the record entry that would let a later reviewer reconstruct the observation without relying on the technician's memory.
stimulus.note: The task is to preserve the measurement together with the context needed to understand who measured what, where/for which material, when, and with which instrument.

choices: “2.1” because the number itself is the main measurement evidence.
“2.1 good” because the qualifier explains that the result was acceptable.
“EC 2.1 mS/cm, Batch B17 input solution, 14:05, Meter M4, operator initials.”
“Normal reading” because the controlled target already defines the expected value.
rationale: A reconstructable measurement records not only the value but also what was measured, the unit, which material or sample it applies to, when it was taken, which instrument was used, and who recorded it. That context lets a later reviewer interpret the observation without relying on memory.
